SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #1 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these people is most likely to use a compass? (1 mark)
   A. A sailor
   B. A tailor
   C. A cook
   D. A baby

2. Which direction is directly opposite to north? (1 mark)
   A. North-east
   B. West
   C. East
   D. South

3. In the morning, your shadow falls towards which direction? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. The sun
   C. West
   D. Nowhere

4. Which of these counties has a coast on the Indian Ocean? (1 mark)
   A. Nyeri
   B. Kilifi
   C. Kitui
   D. Nakuru

5. Which county contains the capital city of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Nairobi
   B. Kitui
   C. Kisumu
   D. Nakuru

6. Which county has a neighbouring county called Kiambu to its north? (1 mark)
   A. Turkana
   B. Mombasa
   C. Nairobi
   D. Kisumu

7. What is a physical feature? (1 mark)
   A. A building made by people
   B. A natural feature on the surface of the Earth
   C. A road
   D. A market

8. On a physical map, what colour is used for water? (1 mark)
   A. Brown
   B. Red
   C. Black
   D. Blue

9. Which of these is a physical feature? (1 mark)
   A. A school
   B. A road
   C. A lake
   D. A bridge

10. What is weather? (1 mark)
   A. The number of months in a year
   B. The size of a county
   C. The height of a mountain
   D. How the air is on a particular day

11. Which of these places is likely to be coldest in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. The slopes of Mount Kenya
   B. A low dry plain
   C. A beach
   D. The coast

12. Which clothing is most suitable in the cold season? (1 mark)
   A. Sandals only
   B. Light shorts only
   C. Swimming costumes
   D. Sweaters and jackets

13. What is the difference between a museum and a cultural centre? (1 mark)
   A. There is no difference
   B. A cultural centre has no dances
   C. A museum is always outdoors
   D. A museum mainly keeps objects, a cultural centre shows living culture

14. What is a monument? (1 mark)
   A. A river
   B. A structure built to remember a person or event
   C. A bus
   D. A market

15. Which is the best source of information about a historic place near you? (1 mark)
   A. A resource person such as an elder or a guide
   B. A rumour
   C. A guess
   D. An advert for soap

16. Which statement is true? (1 mark)
   A. Only farming is important
   B. All useful jobs are important
   C. Only doctors are important
   D. Small jobs do not matter

17. What is trade? (1 mark)
   A. Buying and selling goods
   B. Playing games
   C. Growing crops only
   D. Building houses

18. Why must a key be included on a dot map? (1 mark)
   A. So that colours are hidden
   B. So that the map is longer
   C. So that people know what each dot stands for
   D. So that it looks old

19. What do we call an area where many people live close together? (1 mark)
   A. Empty
   B. Densely populated
   C. Wild
   D. Sparsely populated

20. Which is the best way to show population on a map using dots? (1 mark)
   A. Draw dots where people live and give a key for what a dot means
   B. Write the county name only
   C. Draw a river
   D. Colour the whole map blue

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Give three reasons why historic built environments are important. (3 marks)

22. Explain why we say that the compass is useful in a county. (5 marks)

23. State three ways in which physical features are important to people. (3 marks)

24. Name two landforms and two water features. (4 marks)

25. List four rules that visitors should follow at a historic place. (4 marks)

26. A dot map has 1 dot for every 1,000 people. A town has 12 dots and a dry area has 2 dots. How many more people live in the town? Show your working. (3 marks)

27. Explain how you can find east in the morning without a compass. (2 marks)

28. Draw a weather chart for three days: sunny, rainy, cloudy. Add a key. (3 marks)

29. Give three ways in which the dry season affects people's activities. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #1 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — A sailor
   Sailors use compasses to find direction at sea.

2. D — South
   North and south are opposite each other on the compass rose.

3. C — West
   The sun is in the east in the morning, so shadows point west.

4. B — Kilifi
   Kilifi lies along the coast.

5. A — Nairobi
   Nairobi County contains Kenya's capital city.

6. C — Nairobi
   Kiambu lies to the north of Nairobi County.

7. B — A natural feature on the surface of the Earth
   Physical features such as mountains and rivers are natural.

8. D — Blue
   Blue is used for lakes, rivers and the ocean.

9. C — A lake
   A lake is natural. The others are built by people.

10. D — How the air is on a particular day
   Weather describes sun, rain, wind and temperature at a given time.

11. A — The slopes of Mount Kenya
   High places are colder than low places.

12. D — Sweaters and jackets
   Warm clothing keeps us comfortable when it is cold.

13. D — A museum mainly keeps objects, a cultural centre shows living culture
   Cultural centres let visitors see and take part in living culture.

14. B — A structure built to remember a person or event
   Monuments remind people of important people or events.

15. A — A resource person such as an elder or a guide
   Elders and guides know the true story of the place.

16. B — All useful jobs are important
   Every worker contributes to the community.

17. A — Buying and selling goods
   Trade is buying and selling.

18. C — So that people know what each dot stands for
   Without a key we cannot read the dots.

19. B — Densely populated
   Dense means crowded.

20. A — Draw dots where people live and give a key for what a dot means
   A dot map needs a clear key.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: They teach us history, they give us identity and pride, and they bring tourists and income.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason.

22. (5 marks)
   Answer: It helps us to find our way. It helps mapmakers to draw maps. It helps us to describe where places are. It helps drivers and sailors to travel. It helps us to plan journeys.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point, up to 5.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give water, they provide fish and food, and they attract visitors. Accept farming land or electric power.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Landforms: mountain and valley (or hill, plain, plateau). Water features: lake and river (or waterfall, ocean).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Do not litter, do not write on walls, do not climb or touch old structures, and listen to the guide.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct rule.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: 10,000 more people.
   Working / marking points: 12 x 1,000 = 12,000; 2 x 1,000 = 2,000; 12,000 - 2,000 = 10,000. 1 mark for each step.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: Face the direction where the sun rises. That direction is east.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for using the rising sun, 1 mark for naming east.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Three boxes with a sun, a cloud with rain lines and a plain cloud, and a key that names each symbol.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for correct symbols, 1 mark for the days, 1 mark for the key.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Farmers harvest and dry crops, fishermen dry fish in the sun, and herders move animals to find water and grass.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.
